subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.9 QQBot: long markdown reply is split into N independent bubbles (one per chunk), not a single message

question: Should QQBot keep splitting long markdown into multiple complete messages as intentional behavior, or should safe-size chunks be merged into one visible QQ message via the linked candidate PR?
rationale: Current code and release behavior match the report, but a likely QQBot owner has said the split is deliberate to avoid truncation; automation cannot choose the permanent channel UX and truncation-risk tradeoff.

options.title: Confirm split behavior
options.body: Treat proactive multi-message markdown splitting as the supported QQBot behavior and close the issue plus linked merge PR unless new QQ API proof shows a safe single-bubble contract.

options.title: Land bounded safe merge
options.body: Accept the linked PR's send-boundary merge for replies within the existing 3600-byte safety limit while preserving split behavior for oversized replies.

options.title: Request more live proof
options.body: Keep both open and ask for before/after live QQ evidence that covers the large-table or 80-line boundary that motivated the maintainer concern.

recommendation.title: Confirm split behavior
recommendation.body: Treat proactive multi-message markdown splitting as the supported QQBot behavior and close the issue plus linked merge PR unless new QQ API proof shows a safe single-bubble contract.

likelyOwner.reason: sliverp authored the relevant QQBot channel and chunker history and already gave the current by-design interpretation on this issue.
